title: Latent signal filtering and gradual region evacuation playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We continue to see noisy paging in regional SLO alerts caused by transient spikes and correlated downstream timeouts. On-call teams often escalate to full region failover too quickly, causing unnecessary traffic shifts and cache churn.

Goals:
- Reduce noisy pages by 40% for regional latency/ErrorRate SLOs without increasing time-to-detect true incidents.
- Implement a graduated region evacuation path that can be triggered automatically or manually, with clear circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Ship a deterministic runbook and automation hooks so runbooks can be executed partially (soft-failover) or fully (evacuation) and be reversed safely.

Scope:
In scope: alert tuning for regional SLOs, regional circuit-breaker design, staged load-shedding (gradual evacuation), on-call runbook authoring, and automation integration (PagerDuty / Slack / Runbook Automation).
Out of scope: global capacity expansion, long-term capacity planning, and model-level inference kernel changes (separate workstreams).

Proposal summary:
1) Signal filtering: implement an ensemble filter on SLO alerts combining (a) short-window percentile (p95/99 over 30s), (b) exponential-weighted moving average (EWMA) over 5m, and (c) anomaly score from baseline residuals. An alert only pages if strong signal persists across at least two windows or the anomaly score > 6. This reduces single-sample flaps.
2) Alert hysteresis + silent severity: add a 2-step escalation where the first notification is a low-noise (ops-feed) message with remediation hints; only escalate to pagers after auto-debounce and impact amplification detection.
3) Regional circuit breaker: define three states per region - GREEN (normal), SOFT_DEGRADED (serve read-only/penalize non-critical routes, enable local shedding), and EVICT (active evacuation of traffic to other regions). Transition triggers are based on combined signal score, queue depth, error budget burn rate, and KV cache miss amplification.
4) Gradual evacuation playbook: automated cohort-based traffic shift in 3 phases: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 10-30 minute windows with health-check rollback gates. Provide a manual fast-path for operators to accelerate or abort.
5) Runbook automation: expose playbook as a templated runbook in the RBA engine. When escalation threshold met, RBA opens an incident doc, posts playbook steps to incident Slack channel, executes pre-approved low-risk steps (e.g., set region to SOFT_DEGRADED), and waits for operator confirmation before higher-risk actions (EVICT).

Design trade-offs & rationale: 
- Why not only raise thresholds? Raising thresholds reduces noise but delays detection. The ensemble filter keeps sensitivity for persistent incidents while filtering transients.
- Why staged evacuation vs full failover? Staged limits cache cold-start impact and gives time to recover; it avoids mass cache miss storms that amplify cost and latency.
- Automation safety: default automation stops at SOFT_DEGRADED; EVICT requires operator ack unless confidence is extremely high (e.g., >90% combined anomaly and error burn).

Acceptance criteria:
- 40% reduction in PAGER events for regional latency/error alerts in canary region during 7-day test compared to baseline.
- Playbook executes in staging: automated 5%->25% shift with rollback on failed health gate in 100% of runs.
- Circuit-breaker metrics emitted: state transitions, decision signals, and rollback timestamps visible on the console for 30d retention.
- New runbook reviewed and signed off by on-call rotation and SRE leads.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New Grafana panels: regional-signal-ensemble, circuit-breaker-state, evacuation-progress, error-budget-burn-rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ri-reliability/regional-failover
- Alerts: keep current SLO alerts but change PagerDuty rules to send initial low-noise message to #ops-feed and only escalate to primary pager after ensemble confirm.

Rollback strategy:
- Soft rollback: revert circuit-breaker state to GREEN if health gates show recovery within two windows.
- Full rollback: abort evacuation and issue a coordinated reroute back to region with traffic-shift reversal script. Post-mortem required for any automated EVICT.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for ensemble filter and score computation.
- Chaos tests in canary region: inject high latency and downstream timeouts, validate that only persistent incidents escalate to pager and that staged evacuation obeys health gates.
- Load test to measure cache miss amplification under 25% and 100% evacuation.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement signal filter and low-noise alerting in staging (1 week).
2) Deploy circuit-breaker state machine and metrics.
3) Integrate evacuation script into RBA, test with simulated faults in canary region.
4) Gradual roll to prod: start with non-critical region, monitor 2 weeks, then expand.

Notes & links: see design doc and prototype PR for details.
